verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the windowsill where her tea's gone cold—

outside, a crow answers a crow

that isn't there anymore.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light flickers on by habit—

no one told it

the season changed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She keeps his key

on a ring with no others—

a single tooth

still fitting nothing.
motifs: a lock that no longer exists

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Snow gathers on the mailbox flag

still raised

from a message never claimed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle knows to whistle twice—

once for her,

once for the pause after.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Frost writes her name

on the window, backwards—

meant to be read from outside.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She leaves the porch light burning

into noon—

a small sun that forgets to set.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone else must trim the wick,

so I let it burn—

my hands full of other people's mornings.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dishes stack themselves by evening,

a small congregation—

waiting for someone to say grace.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I wipe the counter clean

for the third time today—

as if forgiveness were a surface.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle forgets nothing,

whistles anyway—

I let it scream till someone answers.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone finally comes running,

turns off the flame—

not for me, but for the silence after.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The window holds the last light

a little longer than it should—

I let it, too, before I close the blinds.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Dust settles on the sill

where the light just was—

I write my name there, then rub it out.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The floor remembers every footstep

better than I do—

I walk soft anyway, just in case.
